item.title: Ashton Jeanty says his ankle feels "really good" and is "super excited" to play Sunday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty expects to play in Sunday's season opener against the Dolphins.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty expects to play in Sunday's season opener against the Dolphins.

Jeanty said his ankle feels "really good" and he is "super excited" to get back on the field.

The second-year player practiced fully again Thursday, his second practice back since injuring his ankle Aug. 23 in a training camp practice.

"Any time away from the game, it’s tough," Jeanty said, via Ryan McFadden of ESPN. "But to get back out there, mainly with the guys, man, it felt good."

The injury appeared worse than it was when it happened, as Jeanty went down while attempting to catch a low pass from Kirk Cousins. But it wasn't, and Jeanty said he knew pretty quickly afterward that he would play against the Dolphins in Week 1.

"I knew it wasn't anything too bad, even though I couldn't put pressure on my foot," Jeanty said in speaking to reporters for the first time since his injury. "I figured it wouldn't be anything that's too long term."

item.title: Former NFL player LeShon Johnson sentenced to five years in prison for dog fighting
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Former NFL running back LeShon Johnson has been sentenced to 60 months in federal prison after he was convicted of six felonies related to dog fighting.
item.content:encoded:
Former NFL running back LeShon Johnson has been sentenced to 60 months in federal prison after he was convicted of six felonies related to dog fighting.

Authorities seized 190 dogs from Johnson's property, the most dogs ever seized from any individual in a federal dog fighting investigation. This is Johnson's second dog fighting conviction; he was also convicted of state dog fighting charges in Oklahoma in 2004.

“LeShon Johnson continued to traffic dogs for illegal fighting despite a 2004 state conviction for similar conduct,” said Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson. “We are grateful to our colleagues at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma and the FBI for partnering with ENRD to bring this repeat offender to justice and to the U.S. Marshals Service for executing the biggest rescue operation of its kind.”

The Department of Justice says Johnson made hundreds of thousands of dollars through his dog fighting operation, selling dogs he described as fighting champions, selling puppies he said were bred to be fighting champions, and charging stud fees to other dog fighters so that his champion males could breed with their females.

The 55-year-old Johnson was a third-round pick of the Packers in 1994 and also played for the Cardinals and Giants before finishing his pro football career with the XFL's Chicago Enforcers.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. remains limited, and Mike McCarthy won't say whether the CB will play
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Steelers have only one player on their injury report, but it is a big name.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers have only one player on their injury report, but it is a big name. Joey Porter Jr. was limited for a second consecutive day, and coach Mike McCarthy isn't giving away anything about the cornerback's availability for Sunday.

“The plan for Joey today is still working through the ramp-up stage, based on what he accomplished yesterday,” McCarthy said, via Alan Saunders of steelersnow.com. “ I understand the interest of who’s going to play and who’s not going to play, but I think clearly that’s something that I’m not going to get into for the competition of the game.”

Porter is listed with a back injury, but he is also seeking a long-term extension before the start of the season.

Porter has not committed to playing without an agreement, and the Steelers have a team policy not to negotiate once the season starts. He missed all of training camp on the active/physically unable to perform list before passing a physical and being added to the roster when the limit moved from 90 to 53.

Porter is due to make $3.924 million in 2026 and wants a deal commensurate with those of Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez.

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers estimated as full practice participant
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Ravens did not hold a full practice on Thursday, but their estimated practice report included an encouraging upgrade.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens did not hold a full practice on Thursday, but their estimated practice report included an encouraging upgrade.

The team lists wide receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) as a full participant after he was limited Wednesday.

Until this week, Flowers had not practiced since joint practices with the Vikings on Aug. 19-20 due to a minor hamstring injury. The Ravens have been deliberate in his return, but Flowers told reporters Wednesday that he is fully recovered.

"I feel great. I feel better than ever," Flowers said, via Ryan Mink of the team website. "I am ready to play football. I feel like we have been off for a while. Our season ended a bit early last year, so we had an extended break. We're just ready to go."

Flowers' status was the only change to the Ravens' practice report.

Linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee), defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) and wide receiver Devontez Walker (groin) remained limited a second day. Madubuike and Buchanan are still working their way back from season-ending injuries.

item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have made a few roster moves in advance of their Week 1 matchup against the Rams.

The club announced that defensive lineman Alfred Collins has been placed on injured reserve.

This was an expected move after Collins suffered a torn patellar tendon during practice in Australia this week. He will be out for the 2026 season.

Additionally, the team has elevated receiver KhaDarel Hodge and defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo for the game. It’s a proverbial revenge game for both Hodge and Okoronkwo, who both entered the league with the Rams in 2018.

item.title: Josh Jacobs remains on Commissioner’s Exempt list while NFL reviews his case
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property to resolve the criminal charges he was facing, but the NFL's disciplinary process has not resolved the case.
item.content:encoded:
Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property to resolve the criminal charges he was facing, but the NFL's disciplinary process has not resolved the case.

The league has confirmed that its review of Jacobs' conduct, which could potentially result in a suspension, is ongoing.

"We have been closely monitoring all developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy. There is no change to his status as he remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt list," the league's statement said.

As long as Jacobs is on the exempt list, he cannot practice or play but does get paid. If he is suspended, the suspension will be without pay.

Jacobs' decision to resolve the criminal case today would seem to be an effort to get the NFL's case against him over with as soon as possible, so that he can return to the field this season. The league, however, is sometimes slower than the legal system to reach a conclusion about whether a player has committed misconduct that should result in a suspension.

The victim in Jacobs' case was his then-girlfriend. A six-game suspension is the standard punishment for a domestic violence case in the NFL, although the actual suspension could be shorter or longer depending on the facts the NFL's investigation uncovers.

item.title: Lions sign WR Tom Kennedy to their 53-man roster
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said on Wednesday that wide receiver Tom Kennedy would have a role in Sunday's game against the Saints and that comment foreshadowed a roster move on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Lions head coach Dan Campbell said on Wednesday that wide receiver Tom Kennedy would have a role in Sunday's game against the Saints and that comment foreshadowed a roster move on Thursday.

The team announced that they have signed Kennedy to the 53-man roster. Kennedy was on the practice squad and the Lions had an open spot, so there was no need for a corresponding move.

Kennedy has been with the Lions since 2019 and has bounced between the practice squad and active roster a number of times. He has 18 catches for 231 yards in 30 career games.

Kennedy has also seen time as a returner and that is likely the area where he'll contribute to the Lions' cause in the opener.

item.title: Malik Nabers being coy about his availability for Sunday, but says it's his decision
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said it is his decision whether he plays in the season opener on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said it is his decision whether he plays in the season opener on Sunday. However, he is not saying he will play.

He instead referred to John Harbaugh's comments from Wednesday, when the coach said he thinks Nabers is "ready to go, man."

"What Harbs said," Nabers said, via video from SNY Giants.

Nabers is being coy despite a second consecutive full practice. He said it's still possible he might not play.

"That's a possibility. Like Harbs said, they're leaving the decision up with me," Nabers said, adding that it's his career.

Nabers tore his right ACL in a Sept. 28 game against the Chargers. He has previously said he will not come back on a snap count, and it seems like he's trending toward a full return for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

He caught nine passes for 167 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 2 loss to the Cowboys last season.

"I grinded my ass off, excuse my language," Nabers said of his rehab. "I grinded, prayed hard, put in a consistent amount of work. Early, early mornings and late nights. I put in the work, and I did everything that I can to be in this position right now to be able to make the decision to play or to not play. If I am out there, I put in a great amount of work to know that I'm able to play, and I'm able to do exactly what I know I can do and will do."

The Giants' injury report remained the same as Wednesday, with defensive lineman Shelby Harris (Achilles), offensive lineman Bryan Hudson (knee), tight end Theo Johnson (shoulder) and offensive tackle Andrew Thomas (knee) remaining full participants.

item.content:encoded:
Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is bringing one of his players from Seattle to Las Vegas.

Kubiak was the Seahawks' offensive coordinator when they drafted Cabeldue in the sixth round last year. He played in eight regular season games for the Super Bowl champs last year, but was waived ahead of Wednesday night's win over the Patriots.

Colts receiver Alec Pierce continues to be a limited participant in practice this week.

Pierce's injury is officially listed as a heel.

Also on the Colts’ injury report, safety AJ Haulcy (ankle), tight end Drew Ogletree (neck), and center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (illness) were all upgraded from limited to full.

Backup quarterback Anthony Richardson (illness) was added to the report as full.

item.content:encoded:
There don't appear to be any doubts about Jets running back Breece Hall's status for Sunday's road game against the Titans.

Hall missed a couple of weeks with a groin injury, but he was listed as a full participant in practice for the second straight day on Tuesday. Hall said he's feeling ready to go after the unexpected time off.

“It was actually a very good two-week vacation," Hall said, via SNY. "I could have been out there a little bit earlier, but the team — I’m thankful they were very cautious with me. It was a real good vacation and I feel really fresh now."

The Jets' entire injury report was unchanged from Wednesday. Linebacker Joseph Ossai (foot) and wide receiver Tim Patrick (groin) remained off the field while rookie cornerback DeAngelo Ponds (calf) was limited. Running back Isaiah Davis (knee) and tight end Kenyon Sadiq (groin) joined Hall as full participants.

item.title: Romeo Doubs on his no-catch, big-drop game: I'll be better moving forward
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Wide receiver Romeo Doubs arrived in New England on a four-year, $68 million free-agency deal.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Romeo Doubs arrived in New England on a four-year, $68 million free-agency deal. The Patriots didn't get anything out of him in Week 1.

Doubs had no catches on three targets and one big drop in the 13-10 loss to Seattle.

“I just wasn’t locked in,” Doubs said postgame, via Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald. “That’s all. I mean, the video speaks for itself. I’ll be better moving forward.”

It marked the fifth time Doubs has gone without a catch in a game in his five seasons.

Doubs was wide open on a pass that hit him in the hands in the fourth quarter of a tie game. It would have been at least a 33-yard gain, but Doubs dropped Drake Maye's pass. Maye threw an interception on the next play, setting up the Seahawks' game-winning field goal.

“I just put that on my end,” Doubs said. “I’ll just be able to move forward. That had nothing to do with Drake [Maye]. That was 150 percent me, and I’ll be better.”

Right tackle Jawaan Taylor (knee) and defensive end Za'Darius Smith (shoulder) did not participate in practice. Offensive lineman Kyle Hinton (knee) was a full participant.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes: I’m a competitor, I signed up for this, I’m going to go out and play football
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Patrick Mahomes says he's ready.
item.content:encoded:
Patrick Mahomes says he's ready.

While the Chiefs' quarterback suffered a torn ACL in mid-December, he is set to start Monday night’s game against the Broncos to begin the 2026 season.

“This has always been the goal — to get out there and play Week 1,” Mahomes said in his Thursday press conference. “It was a long offseason, a lot of work, a lot of great people around me — trainers, [my wife] Brittany, my family supporting me.

“But now we get to go out there and play the sport that I love. So, super excited. I mean, to get to play at Arrowhead against a great opponent, and go out there and be myself.”

Mahomes mentioned being himself on the field several times, which signals his readiness to utilize his legs whenever he feels he needs to. He noted a couple of moments in practice where he felt like he was back — precisely because he wasn’t thinking about his knee. One was a fourth-down play where he took off running and the other was when he was accidentally hit from behind.

“Every coach was freaking out, but I was like, I’m glad — someone hit me and I didn’t just crumble,” Mahomes said. “Stuff like that is good for me. And so now it’s just about going out there and playing the game.”

Those are moments where Mahomes has gotten the feeling that he can go out and execute.

“I’ve built up the strength, I’ve built up all the days of rehab so I can be myself,” Mahomes said. “I’m going to keep myself out of harm’s way like I always will — not trying to take big hits and stuff like that. But I’m a competitor. I signed up for this, and I’m going to go out and play football. I think that’s how I’ve always rolled, no matter what it is. That’s how I’ll probably roll the rest of my career.

“I think that’s what makes me who I am, is that I just love competing,” Mahomes added. “Playing quarterback is one thing. But you’ve got to love competing to have success in this league. You see that with the guys around this league nowadays. I’ll try not to lay any blocks unless it’s needed. But other than that, I’m going to go out and be myself and play football. We’ve built up all this strength over the offseason for that, so why not go out and maximize it?”

Mahomes and the Chiefs will certainly be tested with Monday night’s matchup against the division-rival Broncos. Denver led the league with 68 sacks last season, which was only four sacks below the record of ’72, which was set by the 1984 Bears.

item.title: Puka Nacua has commenced the steps toward complying with a diversion program
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When the NFL placed several players on paid leave to start the season, the list did not include Rams receiver Puka Nacua.
item.content:encoded:
When the NFL placed several players on paid leave to start the season, the list did not include Rams receiver Puka Nacua. And for good reason; although he has been sued for allegedly biting a woman on New Year's Eve, no criminal charges have been filed.

That does not remove entirely the possibility that Nacua will be suspended at some point during the 2026 season.

Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Nacua has commenced the steps required to resolve potential misdemeanor charges through a diversion program. The specific procedure being utilized under California law does not entail an agreement to do so in advance. Instead, the person embarks on the process of fulfilling the requirements. If/when he does, the charge will be simultaneously acknowledged and dismissed.

The situation lands in a gray area under the Personal Conduct Policy. The policy connects a violation to the "disposition of a criminal proceeding." The policy defines that term to include "adjudication of guilt or admission to a criminal violation; a plea to a lesser included offense; a plea of nolo contendere or no contest; or the disposition of the proceeding through a diversionary program, deferred adjudication, disposition of supervision, conditional dismissal, adjournment in contemplation of dismissal, pretrial intervention or similar arrangement."

The question becomes whether the commencement of compliance with the terms of a diversionary program fall within that definition, or whether the violation arises only after the full program is completed.

In other situations, entry into a diversionary program has triggered discipline under the policy, before the steps were satisfied. In Nacua's case, it can be argued that, since there are no charges and no formal agreement, discipline should wait. The league could view that as a matter of semantics.

Obviously, there's an understanding as to what will happen if Nacua complies with the terms of the diversion arrangement; he won't face misdemeanor charges. The only question is whether the league will review the situation for discipline before, or after, he achieves full compliance.

The NFL has not yet responded to a specific inquiry whether commencement of the compliance process is enough to activate discipline. If not, Nacua likely will be available throughout the 2026 season. If so, a suspension could still happen this year.

item.title: Chris Johnson acknowledges possible link between his football career and his ALS
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In late June, former NFL running back Chris Johnson disclosed that he suffers from ALS.
item.content:encoded:
In late June, former NFL running back Chris Johnson disclosed that he suffers from ALS. The announcement came during an interview with Good Morning America.

The segment raised questions about Michael Strahan's decision to not ask Johnson whether he believes football contributed to his ALS, and regarding the failure of the narration accompanying the interview or the discussion following it to mention the link between football and ALS.

The connection is undeniable; for example, an ALS diagnosis triggers automatic eligibility for participation in the concussion settlement, for qualified retired players.

In a letter to his children posted at The Players Tribune, Johnson acknowledges the possibility that football caused his ALS.

"I’ve seen a lot of neurologists at this point and been to basically every major ALS clinic in the country, and in my experience, as soon as you say you played football it’s like, 'Ahh, OK,'" Johnson writes. "Almost like an understanding, you know? I read one study, and from my understanding, it found that former NFL players were nearly four times as likely to develop and pass away from ALS compared with the U.S. male population overall. That was a shock. And to be clear, your dad’s not an expert, and that’s just one study, and there might be other environmental factors at play. Anybody can get ALS."

He's right that anyone can get ALS. The study to which Johnson refers emerged in early July. The fact that the information came as a "shock" to Johnson underscores the importance of ensuring that football players factor the risk, even if it's small, into their decision to play football.

The risk of immediate injury from football is obvious. The risk of concussion is clear, too, along with the possibility of developing CTE. Johnson's situation, coupled with the recent study, leaves no doubt that playing football introduces an enhanced possibility of eventually developing a disease that will attack the body in a way that no other disease does.

Most players will nevertheless accept that risk, given the good things football can do for them and their families. Still, it's important that they know about the risk.

Chris Johnson didn't. Due to his experience, and his willingness to share it, all players should be aware that the possibility of developing ALS is one of the risks they assume.

item.title: Commanders P Tress Way thinks this will be his final NFL season
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Tress Way has been a member of the Commanders for more than a decade, but it sounds like they're going to have to start planning for life without him.
item.content:encoded:
Tress Way has been a member of the Commanders for more than a decade, but it sounds like they're going to have to start planning for life without him.

Way will begin his 13th season with the team on Sunday and he announced on Thursday that he expects it to be his final one as an NFL player.

"I am pretty sure this is gonna be my last season," Way said, via Nicki Jhabvala of TheAthletic.com.

Way joined the Commanders in 2014 after being waived by the Bears and he has appeared in every game for the team over the last 12 years. He is a three-time Pro Bowler and was named a second-team All-Pro in 2019. He is currently tied for fifth in games played in franchise history and will be No. 3 on the list if he plays in every game this season.

item.title: Mike Vrabel: Drake Maye will learn from it, hopefully we'll be better for it in the end
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Though Patriots quarterback Drake Maye’s poor fourth quarter downed the Patriots in Wednesday’s season-opener against the Seahawks, head coach Mike Vrabel expressed confidence that the young signal-caller will be better going forward.
item.content:encoded:
Though Patriots quarterback Drake Maye’s poor fourth quarter downed the Patriots in Wednesday’s season-opener against the Seahawks, head coach Mike Vrabel expressed confidence that the young signal-caller will be better going forward.

While Maye’s decision-making, timing, and accuracy may have been issues for his first two picks in the fourth quarter, his third was the most troubling given the game situation. Vrabel noted that before the fateful interception, the situation had been detailed to Maye by the coaching staff.

“If it’s there, obviously we want to try to be aggressive,” Vrabel said. “But if not, we’re not losing any yards. And certainly don’t want to give them a chance to make a play. So, that was the conversation that went in.”

“Everything in the passing game is built on timing, built on protection,” Vrabel added "And so, again, if it’s not where you want it, in the timing of that particular play, and protection — just have to throw it away and say, ‘Can’t win it on this throw.’ Drake will learn from it. We’ll all learn from it. And, hopefully, we’ll be better for it in the end.”

Vrabel noted that the Patriots have seen Maye make good decisions with the football and feel like that will continue in the future.

“[W]hen you’re the quarterback or you have the ball in your hands, those things just get magnified — those decisions and the timings and all those other things,” Vrabel said. “We’ve seen Drake perform at an extremely high level and I anticipate him continuing to do that and going that as we move forward.”

What the Patriots don’t want is for Maye to get too reckless. While Maye can make off-schedule plays, it’s important to perform things within the structure and timing of the offense.

“[T]here’s one guy with the ball and he gets to make the decisions, and we trust Drake to do that,” Vrabel said. “So I wouldn’t say that we should allow reckless play, because then it’s just scattered and guys are in different gaps and guys do whatever they want. There’s a scheme to the play and the players have to — we talk about bringing the picture to life. We’ve done that a lot and we’ll continue to do it.

“I think he knows the difference, and I think most of our players know the difference between when they can be aggressive and when they have to be smart.”

item.content:encoded:
While a report indicated Patriots receiver A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain, head coach Mike Vrabel declined to confirm that in his Thursday press conference.

Vrabel noted that Brown's upcoming availability is in question after he suffered an ankle injury during Wednesday night's loss to the Seahawks. But beyond that, the club is still evaluating the receiver.

"We’re running more tests, but we’ll update you here next week," Vrabel said. "Wasn’t able to finish the game, and we’ll continue to evaluate, continue to run tests. But I don’t know if he’ll be available going forward here for the next week, but we’ll see.

"I know he’ll do everything that he can to get back as quickly as possible. And once we get the report, then we’ll figure out what the treatment plan is."

The veteran wideout finished with three catches for 26 yards in his Patriots debut.

item.title: Mike Macdonald: Sam Darnold's hip looks good, but we don't know how long he'll miss
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will miss some time with the hip injury that knocked him out of Wednesday night's game.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will miss some time with the hip injury that knocked him out of Wednesday night's game. But it won't be a lot of time.

Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald said Thursday morning on Brock & Salk on Seattle Sports Radio that testing on Darnold's hip indicated that it's a muscle strain, not damage to the joint, which is not as serious an injury as the team feared.

"The hip is intact and it's good. It's more of like a muscle thing," Macdonald said.

At this point, the Seahawks are still waiting to see how much time Darnold misses.

"How long that is, we don't know yet," Macdonald said.

It seems likely that Drew Lock, who replaced Darnold in the first quarter on Wednesday night and played well in the win over the Patriots, will start Week 2 against the Cardinals. But Darnold may be back soon after that.

item.title: Josh Jacobs pleads no contest to two misdemeanor charges
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jacobs was placed on paid leave by the NFL last month.
item.content:encoded:
Packers running back Josh Jacobs has resolved the criminal charges that led to him being placed on the NFL's Commissioner Exempt list last month.

Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property in a Wisconsin courtroom on Thursday. That court appearance was moved forward from November to today last week at Jacobs's request.

Both that request and Jacobs's plea suggest he wanted to resolve the case sooner rather than going through a protracted time in the legal system before learning his fate. The resolution of the case opens the door for the league to take disciplinary action via a suspension, which would cost Jacobs money while providing a timeline for his return to the team.

Per multiple reports from the hearing, the court ordered Jacobs to to avoid contact with the victim, receive counseling, remain under supervision of criminal justice officials, and pay restitution to the victim as part of accepting his plea.

item.title: Report: Sam Darnold is expected to miss time, MRI under review
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Signs continue to indicate that Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold suffered a major injury during Wednesday's season opener.
item.content:encoded:
Signs continue to indicate that Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold suffered a major injury during Wednesday's season opener.

After undergoing a CT scan and X-Rays on Wednesday night, Darnold underwent an MRI on Thursday morning that is under review, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports. Darnold is expected to miss some time, but Schefter reports the team believes it "dodged a bullet."

Darnold was sacked on the fifth play from scrimmage in Wednesday night’s game and came off the field with a visible limp. He was examined in the sideline medical tent before going up to the locker room for further evaluation. He was then transported to a local hospital to undergo a CT scan.

Head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame that Darnold did not suffer a fracture, which was positive news.

Drew Lock played in Darnold’s stead and helped lead Seattle to victory. Second-year QB Jalen Milroe is also on Seattle’s 53-man roster.

The Seahawks will be on the road to face the Cardinals in Week 2.

item.title: "Strong possibility" Tua Tagovailoa will be cut, if/when benched
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Sunday, Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa returns to the place where he made his last start with the Dolphins.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa returns to the place where he made his last start with the Dolphins. And he's the starter, for now, with his new team.

He essentially won the job by default, prevailing in a competition for which the other primary contender has yet to be able to truly compete. It seems to be a given that, once Michael Penix Jr. believes he's able to play and, more importantly, to protect himself and his surgically-repaired knee while playing, Penix will take over.

For now, Tua has a chance to fend off a benching. If he can't, he may not be able to fend off a termination.

There is, we're told, a "strong possibility" Tua will be released if/when he's replaced. The chance of that happening will increase if he eventually yields not to Penix but to veteran Cooper Rush, who has 16 NFL starts under his belt.

The Falcons signed Tagovailoa to a one-year, $1.21 million contract. It technically becomes fully guaranteed as CBA-mandated termination pay, if he's on the Week 1 roster. But with the Dolphins owing him $54 million minus whatever he earns elsewhere in 2026, he could choose to forgo the termination pay from Atlanta — especially since it's a one-time-only benefit.

Even if the Falcons have to pay his salary, it's a minuscule investment. And it was worth rolling the dice; last year, Tua led the Dolphins to a convincing win over the Falcons in Atlanta.

This year, something is off. It's been obvious when he played in the preseason.

If/when Tagovailoa is released, he'll be a free agent (unless the release comes after the trade deadline). The next question would be whether another team would sign him. He'd have to be willing to embrace backup status, and a new team would have to be confident he could function in that role.

The bigger question is whether he can function on the field, if/when he plays. It seems that the league at large has figured out how to stop him from doing the things that made him the NFL leader in passing yardage in 2023, unlocking what was in hindsight a massive mistake by Miami to give Tua a contract in the range of market value.

The more immediate challenge for Tua is to return to Acrisure Stadium and to have a better performance than he did last December, in the game that got him benched and eventually released by the Dolphins. In many respects, his tenure in Atlanta (and possibly his career) is riding on it.
